expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: a 'table isn't empty' test only checks volume, and this incident wasn't a volume failure.

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: COALESCE(revenue, 0) converted those misses into valid-looking zeros. That line is the actual hazard, independent of what test exists.

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Reconciliation check: warehouse revenue sum vs. source-system revenue sum, daily, with a tight tolerance.

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: checked in the pipeline before publish, not after.

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: A data contract on the upstream table — if they can rename columns without your pipeline erroring, the same incident happens again next quarter with a different column.

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: Assert join-key match rate ≈ 100% between the two tables, checked in the pipeline before publish, not after.

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Response addresses technical fixes but makes no mention of the detection/monitoring gap that allowed the problem to persist three weeks unnoticed.

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: States 'code actively converting a signal into noise' but never explains the consequence or WHY silence is more dangerous than a visible failure.
